text:
SHENZHEN, China — President Lee Jae Myung held bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Wednesday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting.
It is their third summit since Lee took office in June 2025, with two previous meetings in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province in November 2025 and Beijing in January.
The leaders will review progress in bilateral relations and discuss ways to expand mutually beneficial economic cooperation, including trade and investment, presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said in a written briefing issued ahead of the meeting.
Attention is also on whether Lee and Xi will discuss possible U.S.-North Korea talks, as U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and referred to a possible role for Xi.
With an upcoming U.S.-China-Russia summit drawing international attention, Lee’s message on Northeast Asian security will also be closely watched given South Korea’s direct stake in the region.
